contentBlocks.text: You've worked with place value and multi-digit numbers. Today, a new unit: real-world measurement, starting with length!

A ruler measures length in inches or centimeters. To measure an object, line up one end with the ruler's zero mark, then read the number at the other end. Measure 3 real objects around you (a pencil, a book, a toy) using a ruler, recording each length in inches. Compare your three measurements — which object is longest?
You just practiced real measurement — using a ruler to find and compare lengths! Tomorrow we'll measure something different: time.

objectives: Correctly use a ruler to measure the length of a real object
Compare the lengths of multiple measured objects
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's place-value and addition/subtraction work.
2. Demonstrate lining up an object with a ruler's zero mark and reading the length.
3. Have the child measure 3 real objects independently.
4. Complete the worksheet, recording each measurement.
5. Close by comparing the three lengths and identifying the longest.
differentiationTips: Struggling: model the first measurement fully together before letting the child measure the remaining two independently
Ready for more: ask the child to measure a fourth object and predict its length before actually measuring
A real ruler and real objects are essential here — this skill doesn't transfer well from an abstract worksheet alone
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a real-world measurement activity — answers vary based on the actual objects measured; check that the child used the ruler correctly (starting at zero) and can correctly identify the longest object.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 2 standard 2.MD.1: measuring the length of an object using appropriate tools, opening this new measurement-focused unit.

generationData.instructions: Measure three real objects with a ruler and record their lengths.
